description: Functional refactoring suggestions (light bulb quick fixes) for F#, built on FSharp.Analyzers.SDK. Over 130 rules covering correctness, performance, idiom and redundancy; every one is Hint severity, so they never gate a build.
releaseNotes:
0.8.22: FR0157's serializer guard reads the VALUE handed to a reflective head, not only a type argument: a record, or a collection of one, passed or piped to `JsonSerializer.Serialize`, behind a field or property (`Serialize wrapper.Items`) or anywhere along a curried call (`Serialize options value`), stands the rule down, since every field of it is read by reflection and a union field would serialize differently. The union a run adds carries the widest visibility of the slots it types - private when they are all private, internal when one is internal or the component spans files, public only when a public one is among them - so a run without --api-changes never adds a public type to a library by itself. Two audit tests that assumed Windows path semantics now pass on Linux too.
 0.8.21: Three defects from the 0.8.20 sweep over thirty-five repositories. The api pass no longer puts cross-project edits back on a false alarm: FCS cannot hand a sibling in-memory assembly data for a project whose typecheck creates generated provided types (a JsonProvider sample), so the sibling silently bound to the dll on disk, built before the edits, and every migrated call site failed against the old signature (CarmelNet's tests); a failed in-memory check is now confirmed by a real build of the sibling before anything is put back, and the referenced project is rebuilt so the next pass reads the sibling against the edits. FR0156 keeps a pair of parentheses where the drain's were an application's own - `Some(List.ofSeq acc)` had become `Someacc`. FR0157 never gives two unions in one file the same name: two records with a `domain` field each got a `Domain`; a field's second choice now carries its record's name (`JobKind`) before the `Kind` suffix.
 0.8.20: Three idiom rules. FR0158 (new) turns a while loop that walks a mutable index while a condition holds - `let mutable line = 0` then `while line < max && blank line do line <- line + 1`, or the countdown - into a tail-recursive local function (`advanceLine` / `retreatLine`) and an immutable `let`; measured level with the loop, where the Seq.tryFind spelling doubled the time and allocated per call. FR0156 (new) turns a ResizeArray that loops fill one Add at a time and the rest of the scope only reads into a list expression: the loops (for and while alike) move inside the brackets as they are - guards, matches, nested loops, lets and the statements around each Add included - and each Add becomes the implicit yield of its argument; List.ofSeq acc becomes acc, and Seq functions, for x in acc and an upcast to seq keep working. Measured in PerfClaims (.NET 10, 1000 ints): 20 percent faster on 30 percent less allocation than the fill-then-copy. A drain that wants an array (an index, Count, ToArray(), Array.ofSeq) stands the rule down, since the array expression measured 1.6x the ResizeArray fill's time and ResizeArray plus ToArray() is the fastest spelling of an array built one element at a time; { "FR0156": { "arrays": true } } buys the shape at that price. The declared element type becomes the list's annotation (Add converted an int literal to int64 through the method call where a bare yield would not), and an element type with subtypes to upcast from (an interface, obj, an unsealed class) stands the rule down. FR0157 (new) turns a closed set of string literals matched by name into a [<RequireQualifiedAccess>] union with a ToString returning the original text. The proof is a flow analysis over the string slots the value passes through - a parameter, a let, a record field, a function's return, a name a pattern binds, plain or option-wrapped - closed when every source is a literal (or a constant, [<Literal>] or not) or another slot and every sink a match, a comparison with a literal, a flow into a slot or a print through ToString; proven from either end, the call sites or a producing function whose every exit is a literal. Every literal source, arm and comparison becomes its case, every annotated slot is retyped, and a catch-all the proof leaves dead is dropped - it stays where the proof found a literal no arm names. A variable pattern spelling a module-level constant's name beside later arms (| us -> under let us = "...", which binds a fresh us and matches everything) is taken for the comparison the author meant, and the message says so. A Result<_, string> is a slot like the others: its Error "..." exits are sources, its Error "..." arms the consumer, the Ok side is not followed. Under --api-changes the apply tool's api pass runs the rule with every referencing project's call sites in its world, so an exported function's literal callers count; where the host still cannot see every caller, the exported function keeps its public signature behind an adapter - a private twin typed with the union, the compilation's own callers moved to it, a wrapper of the old name mapping at the edge (OfString, whose unknown arm is the match's own raising catch-all; Result.mapError string) under a TODO. A %s hole becomes %O and a concatenation operand `string x`; a sentence-shaped literal keeps its words behind double backticks; a record a serializer fills ([<CLIMutable>], a Json or DataContract attribute, the type as a type argument anywhere), a dynamic message, a method call on the string, a function used as a value, a lambda parameter, and a set no producer feeds stand the rule down. The apply tool reads the whole compilation's symbol uses once, indexed by declaration and by position, so the analysis costs a few seconds per project rather than a walk per question. FR0154 is a correctness rule now and rewrites only the miss arm: TryGetValue then a store on a ConcurrentDictionary keeps its match and hit arm, and the miss arm becomes GetOrAdd(key, fun _ -> compute ()), whose add is atomic. Measured at tier 1 the hit path - the one a cache takes almost every time - is 2.1 ns and nothing on TryGetValue against 7.3 ns and a 64 B delegate on GetOrAdd, so the whole-match rewrite of 0.8.12 was a slowdown sold as a speedup; the race it closes is the reason, and this shape closes it at no cost. Where running the factory ONCE matters, GetOrAdd alone does not buy it (concurrent misses each run it), so a factory that calls something carries the hint that a Lazy value - GetOrAdd(key, fun _ -> lazy (compute ())).Force() - runs it once, and a Task, ValueTask or Async value, where the discarded result is a computation already running, gets that note without a fix.

 0.8.19: The build configuration the analysis does not see is no longer a blind spot. A project whose sources branch on `#if DEBUG` / `!DEBUG` / `RELEASE` / `TRACE` gets a second pass under the other configuration, where those branches are the parse tree, and its verification builds both configurations; a referencing project edited by a call-site migration is built in the other configuration too, and the migration is put back when that build fails. A call-site migration (FR0090, FR0091) keeps back a function named inside a configuration region, whose other branch has calls no parse tree holds, and one a string literal names anywhere in the project or its referencing projects - a code generator's template writes calls no symbol table lists (SQLProvider.Fable's CodeGen kept emitting the old parameter order after FR0091 reordered Row.text). The apply tool withholds any multi-line fix whose span covers a #if, #else or #endif line, whatever rule offered it.

 0.8.18: A sweep spends far less of its time in MSBuild and FCS. The compiler-argument query no longer cleans the project (a design-time build with the target forced, in place of the Rebuild that cleaned the outputs and cost a third build to put them back), and the FS3511 harvest that made every compilation recompile is cached per source tree under the local application data, so an unchanged project builds incrementally in a second or two - 28 seconds of fsc per compilation on FunStripe.Core gone. A multi-targeted project builds every framework in one parallel outer build on its narrowest pass, and the next framework's compiler arguments and typecheck run ahead on a checker of its own while the narrower pass sweeps: FCS keeps one incremental builder per project file name, so the frameworks were throwing each other's typecheck away at every switch and could never share one; the second framework's check now costs milliseconds. A file whose only conditional directives are INTERACTIVE or COMPILED - the idiom for a source that also serves as a #load'ed script - is swept once across frameworks like a directive-free file, since neither symbol varies between a project's frameworks. A script's sweep leaves the #load'ed sources a project compiles to that project: Owin.Compression's Script.fsx, typechecked as .NET Core, had written Convert.ToHexString and File.ReadAllBytesAsync into the net48 project's CompressionModule.fs. A proposed FR0155 ([<Sealed>] on internal classes) is benchmarked in PerfClaims before being written: the covariant array store halves and the type test does better, the virtual call does not move.

 0.8.17: A test project's declarations reshape without --api-changes: a project that references xunit, NUnit, MSTest or Expecto exports no API, nothing links to it, so FR0090, FR0091, FR0069, FR0093 and FR0049 treat its own functions as they treat a private module's, while the library compiled after it finds the gate closed again. The project's own type providers are instantiated before any `#r` script is read against a .NET Framework reference set: FCS keeps a design-time assembly by name, welendus's Program.fsx `#I`d packages/FSharp.Data/lib/net45, and every project's JsonProvider was "not defined in 'FSharp.Data'" from then on - four projects skipped in a tree that builds. FR0147 checks every bare name the file uses against what an open brings, not only the uppercase ones: an `[<AutoOpen>]` module brings its VALUES with the namespace, and `open Lib` placed below `open Other.Z` rebound a `helper 4` from Z's to Lib.Auto's, compiling and answering differently; a name resolving to a local is no clash (a local shadows the open wherever it sits); and a union case matched by its qualified spelling (`| Lib.Kind.A ->`) is shortened with the expressions, when it resolves to a case. FR0094 keeps the parentheses inside a `_.` shorthand lambda, as FR0013 did: `configureEndpoint _.WithName("x").WithGroupName(g)` bare applied the lambda to `g`. FR0029 leaves a `return (* note *) value` in place for the plain closure: without the keyword the line's first token stands right of the comment, and the parser reads it as the previous let's continuation. FR0035 asks the typed tree whether a list's element type satisfies `comparison` before turning the list into a `Set`, and offers the HashSet companion (equality only, which `List.contains` already asked) where it does not - a [<NoComparison>] record, one with a function field. A rewrite that fabricates a closure or a computation expression asks the typed tree whether the code it moves reads a byref or byref-like value - a Span, a ReadOnlySpan, a [<IsByRefLike>] struct of the project's own - which no closure may capture and no task { } may hold: FR0034's Option.exists lambda, FR0009's Result lambdas, FR0029's runTail, FR0142's task-returning test and FR0049's taskify all stand down where one is in reach (FR0154 already did; the check is shared now). FR0142 no longer holds a test back for a `static let mutable` of its OWN class: xUnit, NUnit and MSTest run one class's tests one after another whatever they return, so the order CarmelNet's tests rely on - one writes a payment id, the next reads it - survives the rewrite; module-level state and another class's still do. A typecheck that never returns is abandoned after 15 minutes (FSREF_CHECK_MINUTES raises it) and the compilation reported and skipped rather than the run waited on: SQLProvider's DuckDbTest.fsx sat in its type provider's database connection for two and a half hours.

 Earlier versions: CHANGELOG.md in the repository (https://github.com/Thorium/fsharp-refactor/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
